entry.title: CATEomics: model selection and ensembling for heterogeneous treatment effect estimation from high-dimensional omics data
entry.summary:
CATEomics addresses the lack of a standardized and reproducible process for choosing among conditional average treatment effect (CATE) estimators in high-dimensional omics studies, where their estimation errors cannot be evaluated directly from observed outcomes. The R package accepts a SummarizedExperiment, applies common preprocessing and data partitions across R and Python estimators, compares their out-of-fold estimates using proxy losses, supports model selection and ensembling, and returns the resulting CATE estimates to the original object for downstream omics analysis. Availability and implementation: CATEomics is implemented in R and is freely available under the MIT license at https://github.com/matsui-lab/CATEomics.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: MetaboRx: R Shiny application for quality assessment and preprocessing of mass spectrometry-based metabolomics data
entry.summary:
Introduction Metabolomics datasets offer deep insights into biological systems, yet the multi-step analytical workflow, from sample preparation through instrumental analysis, introduces unwanted variation. This variation, including signal drift and batch effects can confound true biological signals. Although rigorous quality control (QC) and data preprocessing are prerequisites for downstream analysis, existing workflows are often fragmented, time-consuming, and inaccessible to non-experts.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: Minimizing data requirements for chemical and material property prediction via cluster-based training set selection
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01076-9 A survey of 100 algorithms across 60 chemical and materials property prediction tasks finds that cluster-based selection of training data outperforms active learning, and a theoretical framework establishes why this occurs in the low-data limit.

entry.title: Ab initio simulation of excited-state potential energy surfaces with transferable deep quantum Monte Carlo
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01065-y Transferable deep-learning quantum Monte Carlo for molecular excited states is introduced. Sharing parameters, an ansatz represents the wavefunction across molecular geometries and states, reducing the cost of modeling potential energy surfaces.

Source: Nature Computational Science · Tags: #bioinformatics #materials-science

entry.title: Scalable physical deep learning using optical dynamics with state-skipping training and single-map architecture
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 05 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01075-w This study presents a scalable, efficient framework for unconventional computing with physical neural networks. It replaces dense connections with uncoupled one-dimensional dynamics, simplifies training, improves performance and reduces resource use.

Source: Nature Computational Science · Tags: #bioinformatics #materials-science #neuroscience
